Spindle sarcomatous cell proliferations are arranged in fascicular patterns (D) (×20) with areas of blastematous, rhabdoid (E) (×15), liposarcomatous (F) (×20) and myxoid components. Tumor cells were non-cohesive with disorganized growth patterns, and little elements of cartilage can be seen (G) (×20).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Panel (a) is an ultrasound showing a solid, hyperechoic mass, which is a direct clinical manifestation of pleuropulmonary blastoma (Type III). B: Panel (b) shows vascular signals (CDFI) within the mass, characteristic of the tumor, supporting the diagnosis. C: Panel (c) shows adjacent lung changes (consolidation) and an anechoic collection, representing local structural involvement or complication of the tumor. D: Panel (d) is a CT scan showing a large, heterogeneous mass consistent with pleuropulmonary blastoma. E: Panel (e) shows histology identifying primitive mesenchymal cells, confirming the specific cellular nature of PPB (primitive blastemal cells). F: Panel (f) shows IHC staining positive for Myogenin, a specific finding related to the tumor's mesenchymal origin, supporting the PPB classification.
